doc.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03

title: Original personnel: Ten Pals, bass, drums, piano
summary: The band picked up Adam Hardy and Henry Turner in Dallas, added bass (Jimmy Johnson) and drummer Fats Martin, and Al Freeman on piano.

bands.name: Don Albert and His Ten Pals

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: It wasn't a very big band there, it was Don Hubbard and his 10 Pals. Well, he put a 10 then. It wasn't even 10 then, we didn't get the 10 until we got to Dallas and picked up Adam Hardy. We picked up Henry Turner, played two bands I've never seen of him before. Oh, well, he was the first one in the band. Yeah, I've never seen a heard of him before in my life.
You didn't have a string bass at that time?
No, we had the first band in Texas to use it. People didn't know what a string bass was. You don't understand how I was playing.
But that was what year? That was in 1929. You got the bass player over there?
No, we got the bass player about a couple of three months after that.
And who was he? The Jimmy Johnson. He's got a nice write up in a new book on Buddy Balbrin.
Well, he was a great man, a great bass player. Oh, yeah.
And let's see, we've got the rhythm covered. Louis Balbrin, did he ever play one job? No, he never played, Stan Lee All-Innes.

Never played one job. Well, we got Fats Martin, somebody told me a good drummer at that story. Oh, yeah. And he came all the way around to the house on the middle. He was like a lag mother. I said, man, this guy came from all his house. But he gave me a good story about how he was going and he was clearing all this vetting out about later that hour. And the guy killed him. I said, well, this guy must be able to pick something anyhow. So try him out.

Who came with at the Astoria? I don't know. Both of them up there? Yeah, they had a great stage in my life. Yeah, well, he recorded with Lee up there. Oh, he did, yeah. Yeah, with Lee and Professor Davy Jones. Right, like I got him.
Yeah. And who was the first piano player?
Al Freeman. Al Freeman. Where was he from? He was from New Orleans. He was from New Orleans. So the band really was New Orleans musicians at the time. Guys that were from there, mainly. No, no, no.
Not originally from New Orleans.
No, but I mean the guys who were there at the time, mainly. We just only picked up a couple.
At all of them, Lee Lewis, we picked up a time party.
I believe I was the only who was in Louisiana, born. In New Orleans, one of them in the band, in the Cotsville. They got the good and the good boys in New Orleans.

You mean New Orleans boys? New Orleans boys. But there were guys that were in New Orleans at the time. Right, right. And what could Frank Justice play at the time? I've only heard him on the record. Some North, straight, some North. He was with straight, reading, travel on the record. I don't try him on the record. And where was he from? Originally he was from Lake Shore, Louisiana.

Lake Shore, Louisiana. I said. And then too, Jack helped us in a lot of ways. He was a strong guy. Helping for God, they helped help us to set up first. Took care of the fighting for the love. I was dancing.
They didn't have any fights out there.

He was dancing, man, to set up. He was right in the line of fire. He was definitely right there with his strong self. Knock out a couple of them. He was really strong about out there. He was really strong about out there. He had a good idea.
